title: Hereditary discrepancy and factorization norms (AimPL) — Problem 1.1: Constructive Komlós

problems.sourceStatement: Find a polynomial time algorithm to find the signs above.
problems.problem: Design a polynomial-time algorithm that, given vectors $v_1, \dots, v_n$ in the Euclidean unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^d$, finds signs $\epsilon_i \in \{-1, 1\}$ achieving the strongest known (Komlós-type) discrepancy guarantee on $\|\sum_i \epsilon_i v_i\|_\infty$.
problems.wordDescription: Banaszczyk's bound $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ for the Komlós problem was originally non-constructive, and finding the signs efficiently was a major challenge. The workshop-era status was a constructive $O(\log \min\{d, n\})$ bound via the partial-coloring algorithms of Bansal and of Lovett-Meka and the convex-geometric algorithm of Rothvoss. Shortly after the workshop the gap was closed: Bansal, Dadush and Garg (FOCS 2016) gave a polynomial-time algorithm matching Banaszczyk's bound, Bansal, Dadush, Garg and Lovett made the full Banaszczyk vector-balancing theorem constructive (the Gram-Schmidt walk), and Dadush, Garg, Lovett and Nikolov gave an alternative multiplicative-weight-update approach. Since then every improvement of the existential bound has been algorithmic as well: the current best general bound $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ of Bansal and Jiang (2025) is achieved by a polynomial-time algorithm. The problem as posed is therefore resolved relative to the state of Problem 1.05: the only remaining gap between the constructive bound and a constant is the Komlós conjecture itself.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Setting. Let $f^{*}(d, n)$ denote the best bound currently proven for Problem 1.05, i.e. the smallest known function with $K(d, n) \leq f^{*}(d, n)$; at present $f^{*}(d, n) = \min\{O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}}),\ \widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)\}$. Problem. Give an algorithm that, on input $v_1, \dots, v_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $\|v_i\|_2 \leq 1$ (rational entries), runs in time $\mathrm{poly}(n, d, \text{bit-size})$ and outputs $\epsilon \in \{-1, 1\}^n$ with $\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n \epsilon_i v_i\right\|_\infty \leq C\, f^{*}(d, n)$ for an absolute constant $C$ (randomized algorithms succeeding with probability $\geq 2/3$ are allowed). Benchmarks. Constructive $O(\log \min\{d,n\})$ (Bansal 2010; Lovett-Meka 2012; Rothvoss 2014); constructive $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ (Bansal-Dadush-Garg 2016; Bansal-Dadush-Garg-Lovett 2018; Dadush-Garg-Lovett-Nikolov 2019); constructive $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ (Bansal-Jiang 2025). Hence the constructive and existential states coincide and the record is resolved up to Problem 1.05. Complete resolution. A polynomial-time algorithm achieving $\|\sum_i \epsilon_i v_i\|_\infty \leq c$ for an absolute constant $c$ (this would also prove the Komlós conjecture). Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) a polynomial-time algorithm whose guarantee is $O((\log n)^\gamma)$ with $\gamma < 1/4$ (equivalently, algorithmic progress on Problem 1.05(i)); (ii) a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm matching a bound of $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d,n\}})$ or better; (iii) a near-linear-time (e.g. $\widetilde{O}(nd)$) algorithm matching $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d,n\}})$; (iv) an efficient algorithm that, given any input, either certifies (via a polynomial-time verifiable certificate) that its discrepancy is at least a constant times its output, or achieves $O(1)$.

literature.title: N. Bansal, Constructive algorithms for discrepancy minimization, FOCS 2010
literature.description: The SDP-based random-walk algorithm that first made classical discrepancy bounds (Spencer's theorem and $O(\sqrt{t}\log n)$ for $t$-sparse systems) constructive.

literature.title: S. Lovett, R. Meka, Constructive discrepancy minimization by walking on the edges, FOCS 2012; SIAM Journal on Computing 44(5):1573-1582, 2015
literature.description: Simpler 'edge-walk' algorithm for partial colorings, matching Spencer's theorem and giving constructive $O(\log \min\{d,n\})$-type bounds for the Komlós problem.

literature.title: T. Rothvoss, Constructive discrepancy minimization for convex sets, FOCS 2014; SIAM Journal on Computing 46(1):224-234, 2017
literature.description: Convex-geometric partial-coloring algorithm (Gaussian projection onto a convex body) that makes all Gaussian-measure based partial-coloring bounds constructive.

literature.title: N. Bansal, D. Dadush, S. Garg, An algorithm for Komlós conjecture matching Banaszczyk's bound, FOCS 2016; SIAM Journal on Computing 48(2):534-553, 2019
literature.description: First polynomial-time algorithm achieving Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ bound for the Komlós problem (and $O(\sqrt{t \log n})$ for Beck-Fiala).

literature.title: N. Bansal, D. Dadush, S. Garg, S. Lovett, The Gram-Schmidt walk: a cure for the Banaszczyk blues, STOC 2018; Theory of Computing 15(21):1-27, 2019
literature.description: Constructive version of Banaszczyk's full vector-balancing theorem (for arbitrary convex bodies of Gaussian measure at least $1/2$), via the Gram-Schmidt walk.

literature.title: D. Dadush, S. Garg, S. Lovett, A. Nikolov, Towards a constructive version of Banaszczyk's vector balancing theorem, APPROX/RANDOM 2016; Theory of Computing 15(15):1-58, 2019
literature.description: Multiplicative-weight-update based algorithm for Banaszczyk's theorem given a suitable subgaussian distribution; also discusses the tightness of the Gaussian-measure threshold $1/2$.

literature.title: N. Bansal, H. Jiang, Decoupling via affine spectral-independence: Beck-Fiala and Komlós bounds beyond Banaszczyk, arXiv:2508.03961, 2025
literature.description: Gives an algorithmic $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ bound for the Komlós problem, the first improvement over Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log n})$, and proves the Beck-Fiala conjecture (discrepancy $O(\sqrt{k})$) for all degrees $k \geq \log^2 n$, together with an $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{k} + \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for every $k$.

problems.verificationNotes: Re-verified on 2026-09-20 against http://aimpl.org/hereddiscrep/1/ and the arXiv listings of the cited papers. On 2026-09-20 the Google Scholar search links were replaced with arXiv/DOI links, the Gram-Schmidt walk paper was cited directly, and the record was updated to note that the Bansal-Jiang $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ bound (arXiv:2508.03961) is algorithmic, so the constructive state equals the existential state.
problems.statusDetails: A polynomial-time algorithm matching Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ bound was given by Bansal, Dadush and Garg (FOCS 2016); constructive versions of the full Banaszczyk theorem followed (Gram-Schmidt walk, STOC 2018; Dadush-Garg-Lovett-Nikolov). The best current existential bound $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ of Bansal and Jiang (arXiv:2508.03961, 2025) is also algorithmic. Any further constructive improvement is equivalent to progress on Problem 1.05.
